trial_court_outcome.reason: Conviction under s.302/34, life imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine with three years default term matches.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court confirmed the conviction; the headnote states this.

final_outcome.reason: Conviction altered to a lesser offence, which matches conviction_modified.

offence_finally_established.reason: Conviction altered to s.304 Part I read with s.34 IPC.

imprisonment_type.reason: Final sentence for Appellant No.2 is a fixed term of two years RI.

imprisonment_years.reason: Two years' rigorous imprisonment imposed on Appellant No.2.

fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs.500 imposed on Appellant No.2.

neutral_facts.reason: Summary covers the incident, witnesses, post-mortem and FIR without names or outcome; facts match the judgment.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory punishment prescribed for s.302 or s.304.

attempt_completion.reason: Victim died from the stab injuries, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death from shock and haemorrhage due to multiple ante-mortem injuries, including knife wounds to chest and waist.

number_of_offences.correct_value: 1 charged (IPC s.302 r/w s.34); 0 finally upheld as charged (1 conviction stands under s.304 Part I r/w s.34)
number_of_offences.quote: conviction must be altered to one under Section 304 Part I read with Section 34 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Count of charged sections is right, but the altered s.304 conviction still stands and is not reflected.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is mentioned.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court found no common intention; the assault was an immediate response to the earlier incident.

motive.reason: Court accepted the response to the deceased's misbehaviour, intended to preserve the women's honour and dignity.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Eyewitness accounts of PW.5 and PW.7 corroborated by injuries, plus post-mortem evidence, are referred to.

witness_credibility.reason: Court said PW.5 and PW.7 evidence was corroborated by injuries but did not by itself establish common intention.

custody_duration.reason: Judgment mentions detention periods but gives no duration.

bail_history.reason: No bail grant or refusal is mentioned.

trial_duration.reason: Offence 31 March 1994, HC 30 October 2007, SC 10 February 2010 match; trial judgment date not given.

legal_representation.reason: Rishi Malhotra for appellants; Manjit Singh and Kamal Mohan Gupta for the State.

investigation_status.reason: FIR by complainant, post-mortem on 1 April 1994, and completed trial are all supported.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Appellant No.1 found to be a juvenile; case referred to Juvenile Justice Board under s.20 of the JJ Act
procedural_irregularity.quote: let his case be referred to the concerned Juvenile Justice Board in terms of Section 20
procedural_irregularity.reason: Juvenility and JJB referral are noted, but the judgment does not say he was decided as an adult.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court confirmation and partial Supreme Court allowance are all supported.

prosecution_argument.reason: State argued Appellant No.2 chased and held the victim, showing common motive, and urged upholding the conviction.

defence_argument.reason: Defence arguments on no common intention, lack of knowledge of knives, and juvenility match the judgment.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Court required common intention for s.34 liability and applied s.304 Part I in its absence.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: V. Sreedharan (relied on) and Hari Ram (referred to) with citations match.

sentencing_rationale.reason: The judgment gives no explicit rationale for the two-year sentence.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Court weighed the provocation from the deceased's conduct and the limited role without common intention.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The court weighed no aggravating factors.

other_sentence_order.reason: Records sent to the JJB, s.428 Cr.P.C. set-off, and 15-day default term are all in the order.
